title: Dimensional modelling: fact tables and dimension tables

videos.script: Every number in a warehouse is a measurement of something that happened. A sale. A stock count. A parcel leaving the building. {{events}} And every measurement is useless on its own. Ninety-five reais means nothing until you know which book, which shop, which day, and who bought it. {{context}} That split is the whole of dimensional modelling. Facts are what was measured. Dimensions are what it is measured by. {{split}} In this lesson Ana builds the first of each, out of the shop's own data. A fact table of order lines. A dimension for books, one for shops, one for dates. {{build}} Then come the rules that stop the numbers lying. Some measures add up across everything. Some add up across shops but not across months. Some never add up at all. {{additivity}} And there is more than one kind of fact table. One row per event, one row per month, or one row per order that changes as the parcel moves. {{kinds}} By the end you can look at any table in a warehouse and say which it is, and what you may sum. {{end}}
